Regardless of this `keep_empty_rows` setting, only data recorded by the Google Analytics (GA4) property can be displayed in a report. For example if a property never logs a `purchase` event, then a query for the `eventName` dimension and `eventCount` metric will not have a row eventName: "purchase" and eventCount: 0.

member.name: P:Google.Apis.AnalyticsData.v1beta.Data.RunReportRequest.Limit
member.summary: The number of rows to return. If unspecified, 10,000 rows are returned. The API returns a maximum of 250,000 rows per request, no matter how many you ask for. `limit` must be positive. The API can also return fewer rows than the requested `limit`, if there aren't as many dimension values as the `limit`. For instance, there are fewer than 300 possible values for the dimension `country`, so when reporting on only `country`, you can't get more than 300 rows, even if you set `limit` to a higher value. To learn more about this pagination parameter, see [Pagination](https://developers.google.com/analytics/devguides/reporting/data/v1/basics#pagination).
